supplementaryReferences.title: South African food part and planting context
supplementaryReferences.quote: Carob pods are excellent fodder and also food for mankind.
supplementaryReferences.doc: C.J. Esterhuyse (1989), Department of Environment Affairs, Agroforestry, pamphlet 412
supplementaryReferences.note: Government guidance identifies pods, severe-frost exclusion, irrigation in arid areas and variation between seedling trees. It recommends grafted material and pollen provision; not every tree has the same crop.

supplementaryReferences.title: Locally tested carob food products and cultivars
supplementaryReferences.doc: Iipumbu (2008), Stellenbosch MSc Food Science thesis, university-provided abstract in FAO AGRIS
supplementaryReferences.note: The primary study tested South African grown pod material, including those named cultivars and an unknown one, and developed food products. This is food-part evidence, not a regional maturity/yield trial. University full-text handle returned HTTP 403 during checking.

care: Harvested product is the pod. Confirm the planting material's sex and compatible pollen; seedling pod crops vary.
Check local frost and water. Food processing needs a suitable method and explicit kept-stock records.
purchase: Use identified grafted material rather than assuming an unknown seedling will match a productive tree. Tylliria, SFax, Aaronsohn and Santa Fe were in the South African food-composition study; that does not rank their farm yield or regional suitability.
